items.body: This guide helps you create a port-forward rule in the router's mobile app for eero.

bullets: Confirm the host Mac is the device that will receive the forward.
Keep the router login open so you can return to the forwarding page if the firmware hides advanced settings.
Have the host Mac's local IP ready: Unavailable on this Mac right now.
Check whether management happens in the router app first; some mesh systems hide forwarding outside the app.
Target device / internal IP: Unavailable on this Mac right now
Recommended protocol guidance: CUSTOM PROTOCOL STRING FOR THIS TEST
Bedrock port: 19132 (usually UDP, when Bedrock/Geyser is enabled)

items.title: Confirm eero is the router doing routing
items.body: If eero is in bridge mode, the forwarding rule belongs on the upstream router instead.

items.title: Open the eero app
items.body: eero is app-managed first. Open the eero app and go to the network settings area.

items.title: Find Reservations & Port Forwarding
items.body: Open Settings, then Network Settings, then Reservations & Port Forwarding.

items.title: Select the host Mac and enter the port
items.body: Choose the Mac running Minecraft Server Controller. Add a TCP rule for the Java port and a UDP rule for the Bedrock port if Bedrock is enabled.

items.title: Save and test
items.body: Save the rule and test from a different network. If nothing works, check whether the ISP modem/router is still doing routing above eero.

items.title: App-first flow
items.body: eero users often think of the network by app name rather than router model. Matching should preserve that later.
If eero is in bridge mode, port forwarding must be configured elsewhere.
If the rule still does not work after you save and test from another network, continue with the matching troubleshooting topics below instead of guessing.

notes: resolvedString(for: .recommendedProtocol) just echoes context.recommendedProtocol verbatim -- it does not call makeRecommendedProtocol internally. The two features are decoupled: a host is expected to call makeRecommendedProtocol itself and feed the result into the context.
